title: The bag on the door
body: My mother hangs a cloth bag on the back of our front door. It is grey and a little old. The rule in our home is simple: nobody leaves without it. We started three years ago. At first I often forgot, and the plastic bags that I brought home filled a whole drawer. My father counted them one Sunday. Forty-one. Now the drawer is empty. The cloth bag we use every week is still the same one. It has carried rice, books, a football and once a small cat. Some friends say one family cannot change anything. Maybe they are right. But the bag costs nothing, and it takes no time. A habit which is easy to keep is worth more than a plan nobody follows.

questions.q: What is the rule in the writer's home?
options: Everyone must clean the drawer on Sunday.
Nobody leaves home without the cloth bag.
Plastic bags must be kept in a drawer.
Everyone must carry books in the bag.
questions.explanation: 'The rule in our home is simple: nobody leaves without it.'

questions.q: What did the father do one Sunday?
options: He bought a new cloth bag.
He threw the drawer away.
He carried rice in the bag.
He counted the plastic bags at home.
questions.explanation: 'My father counted them one Sunday. Forty-one.'

questions.q: What does the last sentence mean?
options: A small habit people can keep is better than a big plan they cannot.
Cloth bags are cheaper than plastic ones.
One family can change the whole world.
Plans are more important than habits.
questions.explanation: 'A habit which is easy to keep is worth more than a plan nobody follows.'

title: The lights we turned down
body: Every autumn, small birds fly over our city at night. Our science teacher told us that bright lights make them lose their way. Some of them are endangered. Last October our class wrote a short letter to the office of our school. We asked for one thing: turn off the tall lights on the sports field after ten o'clock. The answer we got was short. "We will try it for a month." In November a teacher who studies birds walked around the field each morning. He found fewer birds on the ground than in other years. The school kept the new rule. It is a small field in a big city. But the sky above it is a little darker now, and the birds that pass over us are a little safer.

questions.q: Why are bright lights a problem for the birds?
options: They make the birds fly faster.
They make the field too hot.
They make the birds lose their way.
They stop the birds from eating.
questions.explanation: 'Our science teacher told us that bright lights make them lose their way.'

questions.q: What did the class ask the school to do?
options: To turn off the tall lights after ten o'clock.
To build a new sports field.
To invite a bird teacher to school.
To write a letter to the city.
questions.explanation: 'We asked for one thing: turn off the tall lights on the sports field after ten o'clock.'

questions.q: Why did the school keep the new rule?
options: Because the students asked again.
Because the lights were broken.
Because the rule saved a lot of money.
Because fewer birds were found on the ground.
questions.explanation: 'He found fewer birds on the ground than in other years. The school kept the new rule.'

title: The roof that makes power
body: Two summers ago our school put solar panels on the roof of the library. Most of us did not care. A roof is a roof. Then the physics teacher put a small screen in the hall. It shows the power the panels make each day. On sunny days the number climbs quickly. On grey days it hardly moves. Now students stop in front of it. Someone always says, "Look, it is a good day today." The screen which nobody asked for has changed something. We know how much light our library uses. We know what a cloudy week costs. The panels do not make the school rich. But the number on that screen makes the sun feel like a thing we can count.

questions.q: What did the school put on the library roof?
options: A small screen.
Solar panels.
A new hall.
A weather station.
questions.explanation: 'Two summers ago our school put solar panels on the roof of the library.'

questions.q: What does the screen in the hall show?
options: How much power the panels make each day.
How many students use the library.
The weather for the coming week.
The cost of the panels.
questions.explanation: 'It shows the power the panels make each day.'

questions.q: How did the screen change the students?
options: They now study in the hall.
They stopped using the library lights.
They started to notice the sun and the school's power use.
They asked for more panels.
questions.explanation: 'Now students stop in front of it.' 与 'We know how much light our library uses.'

title: One river, two lists
body: On the first Saturday of every month, about thirty people walk along our river with bags. They pick up the rubbish they find on the bank. The team keeps two lists. The first one is short: the things that go to the recycling centre. The second is long: the things that cannot be used again. Old Aunt Guo has kept the lists for six years. She says the second list is getting shorter. Nobody knows exactly why. Perhaps the shops nearby changed. Perhaps people saw the bags and felt something. Last month a boy of nine joined for the first time. He asked which list was more important. Aunt Guo thought for a moment. "The one we hope to close," she said.

questions.q: What do the people do on the first Saturday of every month?
options: They swim in the river.
They plant trees on the bank.
They sell things by the river.
They pick up rubbish along the river.
questions.explanation: 'about thirty people walk along our river with bags. They pick up the rubbish they find on the bank.'

questions.q: What is on the second list?
options: Things that cannot be used again.
Things that go to the recycling centre.
The names of the team members.
The dates of the walks.
questions.explanation: 'The second is long: the things that cannot be used again.'

questions.q: What does Aunt Guo mean by "The one we hope to close"?
options: The recycling centre should be closed.
She hopes the list of useless rubbish will one day be empty.
The team should stop keeping lists.
The first list is too short to keep.
questions.explanation: 'She says the second list is getting shorter.' 与该问答呼应,指希望「不可再用」那一类最终归零。
